The 2012 Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council election took place on May 3, 2012, as part of the local elections held across England. These elections were to elect members to the Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council, which is the local authority for the metropolitan borough of Stockport in Greater Manchester, England. 

In Stockport, council elections typically involve electing a portion of the council members, as the council operates on a system where one-third of the council is elected each year over a four-year cycle. In 2012, one-third of the seats on the council were contested.

The main political parties contesting the election included the Liberal Democrats, Labour Party, Conservative Party, and various smaller parties and independent candidates. Prior to the election, the Liberal Democrats had control of the council, a position they had held for several years.

Key issues in the election often reflect local concerns, such as public services, housing, taxation, and community development. However, specific campaign issues from 2012 would need to be researched for detailed insight.

The outcome of the election affected the composition and control of the council, influencing local policy and governance in Stockport. As typical with local elections, results vary significantly by ward, impacting the broader political landscape of the area. 

For the exact results, numbers of seats won by each party, or specific ward results from the 2012 elections, you might need to consult local election archives, news coverage from the time, or the official Stockport Council records.
